newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Profit-taking trims Hungary BUX, MOL hits high.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking trims Hungary BUX, MOL hits high.

text.p: The Hungarian share market retreated on Thursday with a less than half percent fall in the BUX index as investors decided to cash in some profits after a 2.65 percent rally on Wednesday, traders said.
The BUX index finished at a preliminary 6,450.68 points, down 29.73 points or 0.46 percent, coming down from a new record high reached on Wednesday.
"There was some profit-taking but one can see buyers at lower prices," said Geza Raner of Bank Austria-Investment Rt. "There are still many who are contemplating to buy," he said.
Raner added that investors were a little more cautious but doubted that this would last long.
Nevertheless, certain stocks not only bucked the trend but reached new record levels as well.
Among them was the market's highest capitalised oil company MOL which rallied to a new record level of 3,945 forints, before retreating to end at 3,930 forints, up 115.
An other trader said earlier today that the market was expecting an up to 16 percent increase in Hungary's state controlled domestic gas sale price, adding this talk pushed MOL's price higher.
Pharmaceuticals Human was also among the top gainers of the day but it also closed below the day's peak of 3,175 forints, at 3,065, up 75 from Wednesday's close.
An analyst said he was upbeat on the Budapest market's outlook, which was bolstered by strong corporate earnings.

"It remains fairly well supported," said Roger Monson, chief equity strategist at Daiwa Europe Ltd. "I wouldn't expect a large correction even if you have some sort of weakness in nearby markets in Prague or Warsaw."
Monson said the market was benefiting from strong earnings by leading companies on the bourse.
"The story remains pretty much founded on the earnings trends of the leading companies," Monson said.
On Thursday, the chemicals and bank stocks were among the losers, with TVK ending at 3,165 forints, down 20 and BorsodChem at 7,100, down 50.
OTP Bank, a strong gainer on Wednesday, fell 125 forints to 4,545.
Inter-Europa Bank dipped 100 forints to 45,900, although in low volume.
